headline: Allies pledge common cause at St James's Palace
detail: Britain, the Dominions and eight exiled governments sign a declaration in London promising to fight on together and work for a free post-war world.

headline: Soviet mass deportations from the Baltic states
detail: In one night the NKVD seizes tens of thousands of Estonians, Latvians and Lithuanians, including whole families, and ships them in cattle wagons to Siberia.

headline: Operation Battleaxe opens on the Egyptian frontier
detail: Wavell attacks to relieve Tobruk. In three days German anti-tank guns knock out 98 British tanks and the offensive is called off.

headline: Germany and Turkey sign a friendship treaty
detail: Four days before Barbarossa, Ankara agrees a non-aggression pact with Berlin, keeping Turkey neutral and Germany's southern flank quiet.

headline: Allied troops enter Damascus
detail: Free French, Indian and Australian forces take the Syrian capital from Vichy French defenders after four days of fighting.

headline: Germany invades the Soviet Union
detail: Operation Barbarossa: over three million German troops and their allies attack from the Baltic to the Black Sea. Italy and Romania declare war on the USSR.

headline: Kaunas pogrom begins
detail: Lithuanian nationalists, encouraged by Einsatzgruppe A, murder thousands of Jews in Kaunas over several days, some of them in public before crowds.

headline: Finland declares itself at war with the USSR
detail: After Soviet air raids on Finnish cities, Finland joins the German attack, beginning what Finns call the Continuation War.

headline: Białystok's Great Synagogue burned with Jews inside
detail: German Police Battalion 309 herds hundreds of Jewish men into the synagogue and sets it on fire. Some 2,000 Jews are murdered in the city that day.

headline: Minsk falls as panzers close a vast pocket
detail: Belarus's capital is taken six days into the invasion. Around Białystok and Minsk, German pincers trap hundreds of thousands of Soviet soldiers.

headline: Germans enter Lviv; pogroms follow
detail: As the Soviets retreat, NKVD prison massacres are discovered. Jews are blamed, and in days of violence thousands are murdered in Lviv.

headline: Stalin breaks his silence on the radio
detail: In his first wartime broadcast, Stalin calls Soviet citizens 'brothers and sisters' and orders a scorched-earth policy: leave the enemy nothing.

headline: US troops land in Iceland
detail: American forces begin relieving the British garrison of Iceland, bringing the still-neutral United States deep into the Battle of the Atlantic.

headline: Massacre of the Jews of Jedwabne
detail: In the occupied Polish town of Jedwabne, Polish neighbours, under German encouragement, murder hundreds of Jewish residents, most burned alive in a barn.

headline: Anglo-Soviet agreement signed in Moscow
detail: Britain and the Soviet Union promise mutual help against Germany and agree that neither will make a separate peace.

headline: Armistice of Acre ends the Syria campaign
detail: Vichy forces in Syria and Lebanon surrender to the British and Free French. Most Vichy soldiers choose repatriation to France rather than join de Gaulle.

headline: MAUD Committee says an atomic bomb is feasible
detail: British scientists report that a uranium bomb could be built within a few years. The report spurs the American atomic programme.

headline: Germans capture Smolensk
detail: Army Group Centre takes the city on the road to Moscow, but fierce Soviet counter-attacks around Smolensk slow the German advance for two months.

headline: First German air raid on Moscow
detail: Luftwaffe bombers strike the Soviet capital overnight. Muscovites shelter in the deep stations of the Metro.

headline: United States freezes Japanese assets
detail: Roosevelt responds to Japan's moves in Indochina by freezing Japanese funds in America. Britain and the Netherlands follow.

headline: Japan occupies southern French Indochina
detail: With Vichy's consent, Japanese troops move into southern Indochina, putting airfields within reach of Malaya, Singapore and the Philippines.

headline: Göring authorises Heydrich to plan a 'total solution'
detail: A written order instructs Heydrich to prepare a comprehensive solution of the 'Jewish question' in Europe under German control.

headline: America halts oil exports to Japan
detail: The US stops licensing oil shipments to Japan, which imports most of its oil from America. Tokyo's leaders begin to see war as the alternative.

headline: Bishop von Galen denounces Nazi 'euthanasia'
detail: In Münster the Catholic bishop condemns the secret killing of disabled people from the pulpit. Copies of his sermon circulate across Germany.

headline: Soviet bombers raid Berlin
detail: Naval bombers flying from an island in the Baltic make the first Soviet raid on the German capital. The damage is small; the message is not.

headline: Atlantic Charter published
detail: After meeting secretly off Newfoundland, Roosevelt and Churchill set out shared war aims, including self-government for all peoples and no territorial gains.

headline: Hitler halts the T4 gassing programme
detail: After about 70,000 disabled people have been gassed in German institutions, the centralised programme is stopped. Its staff and methods move east.

headline: British and Soviet troops invade Iran
detail: To secure oil fields and a supply route to the USSR, the two Allies occupy neutral Iran. Within weeks Reza Shah abdicates for his son.

headline: Massacre at Kamianets-Podilskyi
detail: Over two days German police and SS units shoot about 23,600 Jews, many of them deported from Hungary, at the town's edge in Ukraine.

headline: First Arctic convoy reaches Archangel
detail: Convoy Dervish delivers British aircraft and supplies to the Soviet Union, beginning the perilous Arctic route around occupied Norway.

headline: Jews in Germany ordered to wear the yellow star
detail: A police decree requires every Jew in the Reich aged six and over to wear a yellow star marked 'Jude' in public from 19 September.

headline: First Zyklon B gassing at Auschwitz
detail: In the cellars of Block 11, the SS tests the pesticide Zyklon B on Soviet prisoners of war and sick inmates. Hundreds die.

headline: Japan opens the Second Battle of Changsha
detail: The 11th Army attacks towards the Hunan capital. By early October, short of supplies and under Chinese counter-attack, it has fallen back.

headline: Leningrad cut off by land
detail: German troops take Shlisselburg on Lake Ladoga, closing the ring around Leningrad. The siege will last 872 days.

headline: Roosevelt orders 'shoot on sight'
detail: After a U-boat fires on the destroyer USS Greer, the President orders US warships to attack Axis submarines threatening American waters.

headline: Kiev falls
detail: German forces take the Ukrainian capital after encircling four Soviet armies east of the city. Germany claims some 665,000 prisoners.

headline: First Liberty ship launched
detail: SS Patrick Henry slides into the water at Baltimore, the first of more than 2,700 mass-produced cargo ships that will carry the Allied war effort.

headline: Babi Yar massacre
detail: Over two days, Sonderkommando 4a and German police shoot 33,771 Jews from Kiev in the Babi Yar ravine.

headline: Moscow conference agrees aid to the USSR
detail: Beaverbrook and Harriman meet Stalin and promise monthly deliveries of tanks, aircraft and raw materials to keep the Red Army fighting.

headline: Operation Typhoon: the drive on Moscow
detail: Army Group Centre launches its offensive against the Soviet capital. Within a week vast pockets close at Vyazma and Bryansk.

headline: Deportations of Jews from the Reich begin
detail: The first train leaves Vienna for the Łódź ghetto. Through the autumn, transports from Berlin, Prague and other cities follow.

headline: Panic in Moscow; Odessa falls
detail: As ministries evacuate to Kuibyshev, Muscovites crowd the stations and offices burn their files. In the south, Romanian troops enter Odessa.

headline: USS Kearny torpedoed
detail: A U-boat torpedoes the American destroyer escorting a convoy south of Iceland. Eleven sailors die, the first US Navy deaths of the war.

headline: General Tojo becomes Prime Minister of Japan
detail: The army minister replaces Prince Konoe. In Tokyo the same day police arrest Richard Sorge, the Soviet spy who warned Stalin Japan would strike south.

headline: Odessa massacre
detail: After a bomb kills Romanian officers in their headquarters, Romanian and German troops murder tens of thousands of Odessa's Jews over three days.

headline: Germans take Kharkov
detail: The Soviet Union's fourth-largest city falls, its factories already stripped and shipped east to the Urals.

headline: USS Reuben James sunk
detail: U-552 torpedoes the destroyer escorting a convoy west of Iceland, killing about a hundred men: the first US warship lost in the war.

headline: Parade on Red Square; hospital ship sunk
detail: Troops march from Red Square straight to the front. Off Crimea, German aircraft sink the Soviet ship Armenia; several thousand wounded and refugees die.

headline: HMS Ark Royal sinks off Gibraltar
detail: Torpedoed by U-81 the day before, the famous carrier capsizes under tow. Only one of her crew is killed.

headline: Operation Crusader begins
detail: The new Eighth Army attacks in Libya to relieve Tobruk, opening weeks of confused, costly tank battles in the desert.

headline: HMAS Sydney lost with all hands
detail: Off Western Australia the cruiser fights the disguised German raider Kormoran. Both ships sink; all 645 men aboard Sydney die.

headline: Leningrad's bread ration hits its lowest
detail: Workers receive 250 grams a day, everyone else 125. Two days later the first lorries cross the ice of Lake Ladoga.

headline: Theresienstadt ghetto established
detail: The first Jewish deportees arrive at the fortress town of Terezín in Bohemia, which the Nazis will later present as a 'model ghetto'.

headline: Japanese carrier fleet sails for Hawaii
detail: Six carriers leave the Kurile Islands in radio silence. The same day Washington hands Japan a note demanding withdrawal from China and Indochina.

headline: Last Italian stronghold in East Africa surrenders
detail: The garrison of Gondar in Ethiopia gives up, ending Italy's East African empire. Emperor Haile Selassie is already back in Addis Ababa.

headline: Red Army retakes Rostov
detail: A week after capturing the city, German troops are driven out of Rostov-on-Don: the first major German retreat of the war.

headline: Rumbula massacre begins
detail: In a forest outside Riga, German units with Latvian auxiliaries shoot about 25,000 Jews from the Riga ghetto on two days, 30 November and 8 December.

headline: Soviet counter-offensive before Moscow
detail: In bitter cold the Kalinin Front attacks, followed next day by the Western Front. The German army begins its first great retreat.

headline: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor
detail: Carrier aircraft sink or damage eight US battleships and kill 2,403 Americans. Hours earlier Japanese troops had landed in Malaya.

headline: Hitler's 'Night and Fog' decree
detail: Resisters in occupied western Europe are to vanish into Germany without trace, their families never told their fate.

headline: Killing begins at Chełmno
detail: At a manor house in occupied Poland, the SS starts murdering Jews from nearby towns in gas vans: the first Nazi extermination camp is at work.

headline: Britain and the United States declare war on Japan
detail: Roosevelt calls 7 December 'a date which will live in infamy'. Congress votes for war with one dissenting voice.

headline: Prince of Wales and Repulse sunk off Malaya
detail: Japanese aircraft sink both capital ships at sea in under two hours. 840 men die, including Admiral Sir Tom Phillips.

headline: Germany and Italy declare war on the United States
detail: Hitler announces the decision to the Reichstag. The European and Pacific wars are now one world war.

headline: Britain conscripts women
detail: A new National Service Act makes unmarried women aged 20 to 30 liable for call-up to the services, civil defence or war industry.

headline: Italian frogmen cripple two battleships
detail: Divers riding manned torpedoes into Alexandria harbour sink HMS Queen Elizabeth and Valiant at their moorings. Both are out of action for months.

headline: Churchill in Washington: the Arcadia conference
detail: Allied leaders agree to defeat Germany first and to create a combined command of British and American forces.

headline: Third Battle of Changsha begins
detail: Japan's 11th Army attacks the Hunan capital again. General Xue Yue prepares a trap around the city.

headline: Hong Kong surrenders
detail: After eighteen days of fighting, Governor Sir Mark Young surrenders. About 10,000 defenders become prisoners; atrocities against the wounded and nurses follow.

headline: Commando raid on Vågsøy
detail: British and Norwegian commandos wreck fish-oil plants at Måløy. Captain Martin Linge is killed. Hitler responds by reinforcing Norway.

headline: Declaration by United Nations signed
detail: In Washington, 26 nations pledge their full resources against the Axis and promise no separate peace. Roosevelt coins the name 'United Nations'.

headline: Japanese troops enter Manila
detail: The Philippine capital, declared an open city, is occupied. American and Filipino forces have withdrawn into the Bataan peninsula.

headline: Siege of Bataan begins
detail: Some 80,000 American and Filipino soldiers, short of food and medicine, dig in to hold the peninsula guarding Manila Bay.

headline: Lindsay Ride escapes from Sham Shui Po
detail: The Hong Kong professor and three companions slip out of the prisoner-of-war camp and, guided by Chinese guerrillas, reach Free China.

headline: Japan invades the Dutch East Indies
detail: Japanese troops land at Tarakan off Borneo, seeking the oil of the Indies. In Malaya, Kuala Lumpur falls the same day.

headline: U-boats strike off America's East Coast
detail: U-123 sinks the tanker Norness off Long Island. Ships silhouetted against unblacked-out coastal towns become easy targets.

headline: Chinese victory at Changsha
detail: After fighting in the city's streets, the Japanese 11th Army retreats under counter-attack. It is a rare Allied success in a month of defeats.

headline: Wannsee Conference
detail: Heydrich chairs fifteen officials in a Berlin villa to coordinate the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews. The minutes count eleven million people.

headline: Rommel strikes back in Libya
detail: Weeks after retreating, the Afrika Korps counter-attacks and drives the Eighth Army back towards Gazala.

headline: Japan takes Rabaul
detail: Japanese forces overwhelm the small Australian garrison on New Britain. Rabaul becomes Japan's great base in the South Pacific.

headline: First US troops arrive in Britain
detail: American soldiers come ashore in Northern Ireland, the first of well over a million US servicemen who will be based in the United Kingdom.

headline: British retreat to Singapore island
detail: The last troops cross from Malaya and the causeway is blown. Behind them lie fifty-five days of retreat down the peninsula.

headline: Quisling made Minister President of Norway
detail: The Germans install the collaborator Vidkun Quisling as head of a puppet government. Norwegians' contempt for him is nearly universal.

headline: Soap rationed in Britain
detail: Fats and shipping space are too precious. Soap joins the ration book in Britain.

headline: The Channel Dash
detail: Scharnhorst, Gneisenau and Prinz Eugen steam from Brest through the Strait of Dover in daylight. All six Swordfish sent against them are shot down.

headline: Bomber Command ordered to target German morale
detail: A new directive makes the homes and nerves of German industrial workers the RAF's main target. Arthur Harris takes command eight days later.

headline: Singapore surrenders
detail: General Percival surrenders to General Yamashita. About 80,000 British, Indian and Australian troops become prisoners, the largest capitulation in British history.

headline: Sook Ching massacre in Singapore
detail: The Japanese military police screen Chinese men across the city and execute tens of thousands judged 'anti-Japanese'.

headline: Darwin bombed
detail: Japanese carrier and land-based aircraft attack northern Australia's main port, sinking ships and killing at least 236 people.

headline: Executive Order 9066 signed
detail: Roosevelt's order leads to the forced removal of about 120,000 Japanese Americans, most of them US citizens, to camps behind barbed wire.

headline: Sittang Bridge blown
detail: To stop the Japanese reaching Rangoon, the British destroy the bridge with much of the 17th Indian Division still on the wrong bank.

headline: Refugee ship Struma sunk in the Black Sea
detail: Turned away by Turkey, the crowded ship is torpedoed by a Soviet submarine. Of some 790 aboard, nearly all Jewish refugees, one survives.

headline: Battle of the Java Sea
detail: A Japanese cruiser force destroys the Allied squadron defending Java. Dutch Rear Admiral Karel Doorman goes down with his flagship.

headline: Paratroopers seize a German radar at Bruneval
detail: C Company, 2nd Parachute Battalion, carry off the key parts of a Würzburg set and a radar operator, losing two men killed.

headline: USS Houston and HMAS Perth sunk
detail: Trying to escape through the Sunda Strait, the two cruisers run into the Japanese invasion fleet off Java and are lost with most of their crews.

headline: RAF bombs the Renault works near Paris
detail: The raid on Billancourt, making lorries for Germany, kills hundreds of French civilians in the surrounding streets.

headline: Rangoon falls
detail: The British demolish the port and oil refineries and pull out. Hundreds of thousands of Indian civilians are fleeing Burma on foot.

headline: Dutch East Indies surrender
detail: Java's defenders capitulate. Japan now holds the oil, rubber and tin it went to war for, and tens of thousands of Allied prisoners and civilians.

headline: MacArthur leaves Corregidor
detail: Ordered to Australia, the general escapes by torpedo boat. On 20 March he tells reporters: 'I shall return.'

headline: Penicillin saves its first American patient
detail: In New Haven, Anne Miller, dying of blood poisoning after a miscarriage, recovers after receiving a large share of the country's tiny penicillin supply.

headline: Killing begins at Bełżec
detail: The first death camp with fixed gas chambers starts operating, receiving Jews from the Lublin ghetto. About 434,000 will be murdered there in 1942.

headline: First mass transports of Jews to Auschwitz
detail: A train of Jewish women from Slovakia arrives on 26 March. Next day the first transport of Jews leaves France for Auschwitz.

headline: St Nazaire raid; Lübeck bombed
detail: HMS Campbeltown rams and wrecks the Normandie dock. That night the RAF burns much of the medieval centre of Lübeck.

headline: Chinese division ends its stand at Toungoo
detail: For twelve days China's 200th Division has held the town against the Japanese advance up the Sittang valley before breaking out.

headline: Japanese carriers raid Colombo
detail: On Easter Sunday Nagumo's aircraft strike Ceylon and sink the British cruisers Dorsetshire and Cornwall at sea.

headline: Bataan surrenders; the Death March begins
detail: About 76,000 Filipino and American troops surrender. Forced to march north in heat without food or water, thousands die on the way.

headline: George Cross awarded to Malta
detail: King George VI honours the whole island for its endurance under the heaviest bombing of the war.

headline: Doolittle Raid on Tokyo
detail: Sixteen B-25s from USS Hornet bomb Japanese cities, then crash-land in China. Chinese villagers shelter most of the airmen.

headline: Pierre Laval returns to power at Vichy
detail: The champion of collaboration becomes head of the French government again, under Marshal Pétain.

headline: Chinese troops relieve trapped British at Yenangyaung
detail: General Sun Li-jen's 38th Division attacks to free the 1st Burma Division, cut off and parched among the burning oilfields.

headline: Baedeker raids on English cathedral cities
detail: In reprisal for Lübeck, the Luftwaffe bombs Exeter, then Bath, Norwich and York, choosing historic towns. Well over a thousand civilians are killed.

headline: Benxihu Colliery disaster
detail: A gas and coal-dust explosion in a Japanese-run mine in Manchuria kills 1,549 Chinese labourers, the worst mining disaster in history.

headline: Lashio falls; Burma Road cut
detail: The Japanese take the railhead of the road to China. Supplies for Chiang Kai-shek must now be flown over the Himalayas.

headline: Dutch Jews ordered to wear the yellow star
detail: From 3 May every Jew in the occupied Netherlands aged six and over must wear a star marked 'Jood'.

headline: British land on Vichy-held Madagascar
detail: Operation Ironclad: commandos and infantry come ashore at Courrier Bay to seize Diego Suarez before Japan can use its harbour.

headline: Huitong Bridge blown on the Salween
detail: Chinese engineers destroy the Burma Road bridge over the Salween gorge, halting the Japanese advance into Yunnan province.

headline: Corregidor surrenders
detail: General Wainwright surrenders the island fortress and all US and Filipino forces in the Philippines. Many Filipino soldiers take to the hills as guerrillas.

headline: Battle of the Coral Sea
detail: In the first carrier battle, fought entirely by aircraft, the US loses Lexington but turns back the Japanese invasion force bound for Port Moresby.

headline: Germans attack at Kerch
detail: Manstein's offensive in eastern Crimea routs three Soviet armies in ten days, taking some 170,000 prisoners.

headline: Second Battle of Kharkov begins
detail: Timoshenko's offensive runs into a German counter-stroke. By late May three Soviet armies are encircled and destroyed near Barvenkovo.

headline: Zhejiang-Jiangxi campaign begins
detail: In reprisal for the Doolittle Raid, Japanese armies destroy airfields and devastate villages that helped the airmen. Estimates of Chinese dead reach 250,000.

headline: Petrol rationing and a women's army in the US
detail: Gasoline rationing begins in seventeen eastern states. Congress creates the Women's Army Auxiliary Corps the same day.

headline: Retreat from Burma ends at Imphal
detail: Ragged and sick, Burma Corps reaches India after a retreat of some 900 miles, just ahead of the monsoon rains.

headline: Mexico declares war on the Axis
detail: After German U-boats sink two Mexican tankers in the Gulf of Mexico, Mexico enters the war.

headline: Rommel attacks the Gazala line; Bir Hakeim holds
detail: The Axis offensive begins. At Bir Hakeim, Koenig's Free French brigade beats off attack after attack for two weeks.

headline: Anglo-Soviet Treaty signed in London
detail: Molotov and Eden sign a twenty-year treaty of alliance against Germany and its allies.

headline: Heydrich attacked in Prague
detail: Czechoslovak parachutists Jozef Gabčík and Jan Kubiš ambush Reinhard Heydrich's car. He dies of his wounds on 4 June.

headline: First thousand-bomber raid hits Cologne
detail: Over a thousand RAF bombers attack the city in ninety minutes overnight, killing several hundred people and leaving tens of thousands homeless.

headline: Midget submarines raid Sydney Harbour
detail: Overnight, three Japanese midget submarines enter the harbour. One torpedo sinks the depot ship Kuttabul, killing 21 sailors.

headline: Battle of Midway
detail: Forewarned by codebreakers, US dive-bombers sink four Japanese carriers. Japan's naval offensive in the Pacific is broken.

headline: Japan occupies Attu and Kiska
detail: Japanese troops land on two islands of Alaska's Aleutian chain: the only US territory in North America occupied during the war.

headline: Lidice destroyed
detail: In reprisal for Heydrich's death, the SS shoots 173 men of the Czech village, sends the women to Ravensbrück and later gasses most of the children.

headline: Free French break out of Bir Hakeim
detail: In the night, most of Koenig's brigade fights its way out through the German lines after holding the desert fort for over two weeks.

headline: Anne Frank receives a diary for her birthday
detail: In Amsterdam a girl turning thirteen begins writing. Within a month her family goes into hiding in a secret annex above her father's business.

headline: German saboteurs land in the United States
detail: A U-boat puts four agents ashore on Long Island; four more land in Florida days later. One turns himself in to the FBI, and all are caught.

headline: Heydrich's assassins die in a Prague church
detail: Betrayed by a fellow parachutist, Gabčík, Kubiš and five comrades fight to the end in the Church of Saints Cyril and Methodius.

headline: Tobruk falls
detail: Rommel takes the port in a day, with some 33,000 prisoners. Hitler makes him a field marshal; the Eighth Army falls back into Egypt.

headline: Eisenhower takes command in Europe
detail: Major General Dwight D. Eisenhower is appointed to command US Army forces in the European theatre, with headquarters in London.

headline: Case Blue: Germany's summer offensive
detail: German and allied armies attack in southern Russia, driving for the Volga at Stalingrad and the oil fields of the Caucasus.

headline: First Battle of El Alamein
detail: At a railway halt sixty miles from Alexandria, Auchinleck's Eighth Army stops Rommel's advance in a month of hard fighting.

headline: Convoy PQ 17 ordered to scatter
detail: Fearing an attack by the Tirpitz, the Admiralty disperses the Arctic convoy. U-boats and aircraft sink 24 of its 35 merchant ships.

headline: Sevastopol falls
detail: After eight months of siege and a final month of bombardment, the Crimean naval base falls. Tens of thousands of defenders are captured.

headline: Deportations from the Netherlands begin
detail: The first train leaves the Westerbork transit camp for Auschwitz. By 1945 about 107,000 Jews will have been deported from the Netherlands.

headline: The Vel d'Hiv roundup
detail: French police arrest 13,152 Jews in Paris over two days, including more than 4,000 children, for deportation to Auschwitz.

headline: Me 262 flies on jet power alone
detail: At Leipheim, the Messerschmitt Me 262 prototype takes off for the first time powered only by its two jet engines.

headline: Japanese land at Gona in Papua
detail: Troops come ashore on New Guinea's north coast to march over the Owen Stanley Range on the Kokoda Track to Port Moresby.

headline: Treblinka opens as Warsaw's ghetto is emptied
detail: The first transports from Warsaw arrive at the new death camp. Ghetto chairman Adam Czerniaków, refusing to supply children, takes his own life.

headline: SAS jeeps raid Sidi Haneish airfield
detail: Eighteen armed jeeps drive onto the moonlit Axis airfield and destroy or damage some 37 aircraft in about fifteen minutes.

headline: Stalin's Order No. 227: 'Not a step back'
detail: After the fall of Rostov, Stalin forbids retreat without orders and creates penal units and blocking detachments behind the front.

headline: Kokoda falls
detail: Australian militiamen of the 39th Battalion lose the village and airstrip; their commander, Lt Col William Owen, is killed.

headline: Janusz Korczak goes with his orphans to Treblinka
detail: The doctor and teacher refuses to save himself and walks with some 190 children of his Warsaw orphanage to the deportation trains.

headline: US Marines land on Guadalcanal
detail: America's first offensive landing of the war seizes a nearly finished Japanese airfield. Coastwatchers on Bougainville radio warning of incoming bombers.

headline: Riegner telegram warns of extermination plan
detail: From Geneva, Gerhart Riegner of the World Jewish Congress cables London and Washington: Germany plans to murder all of Europe's Jews.

headline: Disaster at Savo Island
detail: A Japanese cruiser force sinks four Allied heavy cruisers off Guadalcanal in a night action. More than a thousand Allied sailors die.

headline: Gandhi and Congress leaders arrested in India
detail: A day after the Congress Party demands that Britain 'Quit India', its leaders are jailed. Protests and repression spread across the country.

headline: Churchill meets Stalin in Moscow
detail: Churchill tells Stalin there will be no second front in France this year, and reveals the plan to invade French North Africa instead.

headline: Montgomery takes command of the Eighth Army
detail: Appointed after General Gott is killed when his aircraft is shot down, Montgomery tells his staff there will be no more retreats.

headline: Manhattan Engineer District established
detail: The US Army creates the organisation that will run the atomic bomb project. In September General Leslie Groves takes command.

headline: Tanker Ohio reaches Malta
detail: Five of fourteen merchant ships in Operation Pedestal reach Grand Harbour. The crippled Ohio, lashed between destroyers, brings the fuel that saves the island.

headline: The Dieppe Raid
detail: Of 6,086 men landed, 3,623 are killed, wounded or captured, most of them Canadians. Only No. 4 Commando's attack on the Hess battery succeeds.

headline: Brazil declares war on Germany and Italy
detail: After U-boats sink Brazilian ships off its coast with heavy loss of life, Brazil enters the war, opening its air and naval bases to the Allies.

headline: Stalingrad bombed; Germans reach the Volga
detail: A massive Luftwaffe raid sets the city ablaze and kills thousands of civilians. That evening German tanks reach the river north of the city.

headline: Japanese land at Milne Bay
detail: On New Guinea's eastern tip, Australian troops fight the landing force for two weeks and force it to withdraw: Japan's first defeat on land.

headline: Battle of Alam Halfa
detail: Rommel's last attempt to break through to the Nile fails against Montgomery's prepared defences, his tanks short of fuel and under constant air attack.

headline: The Laconia sinks
detail: U-156 torpedoes a British troopship carrying Italian prisoners off West Africa, then tries to rescue survivors under Red Cross flags. An American aircraft bombs the U-boat.

headline: Germans storm the centre of Stalingrad
detail: General Paulus's Sixth Army attacks into the city. Chuikov's 62nd Army clings to the west bank of the Volga, house by house.

headline: Battle of Edson's Ridge
detail: On a grassy ridge south of Henderson Field, US Marine Raiders and paratroopers throw back two nights of Japanese assaults on Guadalcanal.

headline: Commando raid on Tobruk fails
detail: Operation Agreement, a combined sea and land attack on the port, goes badly wrong. A cruiser and two destroyers are sunk and hundreds of men captured.

headline: USS Wasp sunk
detail: The submarine I-19 torpedoes the carrier escorting a convoy to Guadalcanal. Wasp is abandoned and scuttled.

headline: Commandos wreck Glomfjord power station
detail: In Operation Musketoon, a small team blows up the plant's pipelines in northern Norway overnight. Seven raiders are captured; four reach Sweden.

headline: Great deportation from Warsaw ends
detail: Since 22 July, more than a quarter of a million Jews have been deported from the Warsaw ghetto to Treblinka and murdered there.

headline: British take Madagascar's capital
detail: Tananarive falls to Commonwealth troops. Vichy resistance on the island continues in the south until November.

headline: Japanese pull back on the Kokoda Track
detail: Advancing Australians find Ioribaiwa Ridge abandoned. Ordered to withdraw, the Japanese are retreating over the Owen Stanley Range towards the north coast.

headline: Lisbon Maru torpedoed
detail: An American submarine torpedoes a Japanese freighter carrying 1,816 British prisoners from Hong Kong. Over 800 die; Chinese fishermen rescue 384.

headline: A4 rocket reaches the edge of space
detail: At Peenemünde a German A4, later called the V-2, climbs about 85 km and flies 190 km: the first successful launch of a long-range ballistic missile.

headline: Commando raid on Sark
detail: In Operation Basalt, British commandos raid the Channel Island and take prisoners. Germany claims captives were bound and some killed while escaping.

headline: Germany threatens to kill captured commandos
detail: A Wehrmacht communiqué announces that British 'terror and sabotage troops' will be treated as bandits and wiped out wherever they appear.

headline: Britain and the US renounce extraterritorial rights in China
detail: On the eve of China's National Day, the two Allies announce they will give up century-old legal privileges for their citizens in China.

headline: Battle of Cape Esperance
detail: In a night action off Guadalcanal, US cruisers and destroyers intercept a Japanese bombardment force and sink a cruiser and a destroyer.

headline: Battleships bombard Henderson Field
detail: Overnight, the Japanese battleships Kongo and Haruna fire some 900 heavy shells into the Guadalcanal airfield, destroying many aircraft.

headline: Three Doolittle raiders executed in Shanghai
detail: After a show trial, Japan shoots Lieutenants Hallmark and Farrow and Sergeant Spatz, captured in China after the Tokyo raid.

headline: Cyclone devastates coastal Bengal
detail: A cyclone and storm surge strike Midnapore, killing many thousands and ruining crops. Wartime censorship delays relief, foreshadowing the famine of 1943.

headline: Hitler issues the Commando Order
detail: Captured Allied commandos, even in uniform or trying to surrender, are to be killed. Those taken by others go to the SD. Few copies circulate.

headline: General Mark Clark lands secretly in Algeria
detail: Brought ashore by submarine near Cherchell, Clark meets pro-Allied French officers to prepare the coming American landings in North Africa.

headline: Second Battle of El Alamein begins
detail: At 21:40 about 882 field and medium guns open fire. Operation Bertram's dummy tanks and pipeline have hidden where and when the blow will fall.

headline: Seven commandos shot at Sachsenhausen
detail: Men captured after the Glomfjord raid are executed in the concentration camp, among the first victims of the Commando Order.
